newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU extends British pub, petrol station rules.
newsitem.headline: EU extends British pub, petrol station rules.

text.p: The European Commission said on Wednesday it would extend rules allowing British breweries and the EU oil industry to run exclusive distribution and purchasing agreements until December 31, 1999.
The two so called block exemption regulations allow British breweries to operate tied public houses (inns) and oil companies to conclude exclusive purchasing agreements with petrol stations.
The regulations would normally have expired at the end of 1997.

The Commission on Wednesday launched a debate on how to ensure that agreements between producers and distributors in the EU are not anti-competitive, and the two block exemptions were extended awaiting the outcome of that consultation process.
British pubs are mostly owned by breweries that restrict tenants to selling their own brands and those of one competitor.
The oil industry has insisted that its exemption must be extended, possibly by as long as 10 years renewable, as the only way to ensure the legal certainty needed for long-term investment.

The Commission currently grants block exemptions from article 85 of the EC treaty to sectoral agreements, even if they contain anti-competitive provisions, provided consumers benefit. -- Brussels newsroom +32 2 287 68 11
